response.answer: Catalytically inactive rtPA retains LRP1 binding via structural motifs, independent of proteolysis. This interaction is confirmed through binding assays and structural analysis.

results.title: Shear stress‐independent binding of von Willebrand factor‐type 2B mutants p.R1306Q & p.V1316M to LRP1 explains their increased clearance - ScienceDirect
results.content: ## Journal of Thrombosis and Haemostasis. # Brief Report Shear stress‐independent binding of von Willebrand factor‐type 2B mutants p.R1306Q & p.V1316M to LRP1 explains their increased clearance. https://doi.org/10.1111/jth.12885Get rights and content. Under an Elsevier user license. von Willebrand disease (VWD)‐type 2B mutants are endocytosed more efficiently than wild‐type (wt)‐VWF by macrophages. Recombinant Fc‐tagged A1 domain (A1‐Fc, A2‐Fc, A3‐Fc) and full‐length VWF (wt or mutants thereof) were tested for binding to LRP1 or a recombinant fragment thereof in a static immunosorbent assay. Mutant and wt‐VWF were also compared for clearance in mice lacking macrophage LRP1 (macLRP1−) and control mice (macLRP1+). Binding of A1‐Fc to LRP1 was markedly enhanced by the VWD‐type 2B mutation p.V1316M. Surprisingly, deletion of macrophage LRP1 abrogated the increased clearance of the VWF/p.R1306Q and VWF/p.V1316M mutant. Certain VWD‐type 2B mutations relieve the need for shear stress to induce LRP1 binding. Enhanced LRP1 binding coincides with a reduced survival of VWF/p.R1306Q and VWF/p.V1316M.
